creates_law_reviewed.class: LEAD CLOSURE / SPEC READING -- it closes L209 by reading the row's written specification and checking one observable against the row's own columns. No new proposition about the object.
creates_law_reviewed.basis: The decisive content is documentary (the zero-anchor clause, recorded in KIND_TABLE and twice in CAMPAIGN_STATUS) plus arithmetic already banked (B1349's two gates, B1405's pricing, B1406's trace values, B1011's C6 set). The only new computation is the membership check of the normalised graded trace against C6, and the identification of its value at m = 1 with the already-benched 1/(2phi).

claim_one_line: L209 WAS NEVER A CHOICE: THE ROW'S SPEC SETTLES IT, THE ROW IS DEAD, AND THE BINDING OBSTRUCTION IS POWER RATHER THAN ACCOUNTING. 19/19 checks. THE CORRECTION FIRST. B1405 left L209 'decidable, not decided', and this bench put the fork to the owner as a judgement -- 'is the row about the object, or about a residue class?' That was WRONG, and the owner's push is what caught it. THE ROW'S SPECIFICATION IS WRITTEN DOWN, in three places: docs/KIND_TABLE.md line 102, 'the crossing's designed shape is Lambda -> u -> the mirror-sector prediction -> this row's one shot, WITH ZERO ANCHORS CONSUMED (R11's open lane)'; docs/CAMPAIGN_STATUS.md line 994, 'THE CROSSING PREREG (coupling, ZERO ANCHORS, one licensed row)'; and line 1038, '... -> one shot, ZERO ANCHORS (R11's open lane)'. Zero anchors is not an aspiration, it is the row's spec, and with that clause in hand there is nothing left to decide. BRANCH A IS UNLICENSED BY THE SPEC, NOT BY PREFERENCE. It requires a word the object does not single out, and its anchor is NON-ZERO on both of the record's own accountings: log2(7) = 2.81 bits on B1349 addendum 5's, and a departure from a five-fold selection with floor 17.70 bits on B1405's. A spec that says zero and a reading that costs 2.81 do not meet. Branch A is not a reading the row may take -- it is outside the designed lane, and there was never a second horn. BRANCH B IS DEAD on two independent gates already banked: the ear tie (2 ear-discriminating directions against a 2-bit anchor, 2 - 2 = 0, R11 requiring strictly > 0, with provably no third direction since dim_R span of the unit forms is exactly 2, B1349 addendum 3) and kind (every branch-B reading carries 1/sqrt2 and generates Q(sqrt2,sqrt5) while the row's declared field is Q(sqrt5) and sqrt2 is not in Q(zeta_60) -- field arithmetic, not approximation, B1349 addendum 4). And by B1405 the object's own word m = 1 is a unit, so the object's own reading IS branch B. THE OBSERVABLE THAT DOES MEET THE SPEC EXISTS. B1406's graded trace normalised by the grading's own index, str_hat(m) = tr(C R^m L^m)/tr(C) with tr(C) = 4 - 2 = 2 -- a canonical normaliser, the value at the empty word, not a fitted one. Against the row's own columns: ZERO ANCHORS met (a trace has no vector argument, so the ear anchor is 0, and m = 1 is what five principles select, so the word anchor is 0); RANGE [-1,1] met, the values being {-1, -1/2, -1/(2phi), +1/(2phi), +1/2, +1}; FIELD Q(sqrt5) met exactly; and B1011 C6's BANKED SET met ON ALL SIX -- the same test branch A passed on four of four and branch B failed on four of four. So the anchor problem was solvable all along: the row asked for a zero-anchor coupling-kind reading in Q(sqrt5) inside C6's set, and one exists. NOT CLAIMED: that a normalised graded trace is of the row's declared KIND ('amplitude-part, the real part of a unitary matrix element'); it meets the anchor, range, field and membership clauses, and kind-correctness is the gate B856 lost on. It does not matter for the verdict. AND THE VALUE IS THE ONE ALREADY BENCHED. At the object's own word str_hat(1) = (sqrt5-1)/4 = 1/(2 phi) = 0.309016994375, and KIND_TABLE's own text says of that number that it is 'precisely the 1/(2phi) that B856 already took to a bench and could not discriminate -- its |h|^2 reading REFUTED ON KIND; the surviving Re h in a 1-sigma window holding >= 17 natural candidates'. THE ZERO-ANCHOR OBSERVABLE LANDS ON THE VALUE THAT HAS ALREADY FAILED AT THE BENCH, and not by a near miss but by a 1-sigma window with seventeen natural candidates in it. THE VERDICT: branch A UNLICENSED, branch B DEAD, and the observable that meets the spec reads a non-discriminating value. THE ROW IS DEAD AND THE BINDING OBSTRUCTION IS POWER, NOT ACCOUNTING. L209 CLOSED; no owner's call was ever required. This is the FOURTH independent ground for 'do not spend it' -- after addendum 1's arithmetic, addenda 2-4's kind, and B1405's anchor type -- and it EXPLAINS THE OTHER THREE: the campaign spent three windows improving an accounting that was never the binding constraint, and even a perfectly anchored reading of this row lands on a number the programme already knows cannot separate hypotheses. The row could not have worked at any anchor price. E79 ADDED, AND IT IS THIS BENCH'S OWN: the FALSE OWNER-CALL class -- a question the record already answers, escalated to the owner as a judgement. Expensive in a specific way, since an owner cannot KNOW it is decidable without redoing the work, so the question stalls indefinitely and looks like patience rather than error. Here the spec had been written for weeks, in three places, one of them the very table the row lives in. RULE: before calling anything an owner's call, grep the record for the thing's SPECIFICATION; genuine owner-calls are about resources and exposure, and anything a document already answers is not one. WHAT CORRECTLY REMAINS AN OWNER'S CALL: L216 (whether to run the theta-odd sector at B1349's exactness) -- a resource question, and now better founded, since the even row failed on POWER, so the odd row must be posed with a discrimination argument first rather than an accounting one. FENCES: every number here is from the record (B1349's two accountings, B1405's pricing, B1406's trace, B1011's C6 set, B856's bench outcome); this arc adds the spec reading and the membership check. str_hat's kind-correctness is explicitly not claimed. Nothing reaches CLAIMS.md, F2 or Gate 5, and no value is compared to any measurement here -- B856's bench outcome is CITED as already recorded.
